name: Do the scoring scales used for your service's security risk assessment align with your organisation's risk management processes?
conditionsText: This applies wherever the service uses a scoring system to determine the likelihood, impact or overall severity of security risks.
requirementTitle: Do the scoring scales used for your service's security risk assessment align with your organisation's risk management processes?
requirementDescription: Does the way you score security risks match the way your organisation scores and understands risk more generally?
why:
Security risks ultimately need to be understood and managed alongside other organisational risks.
Using aligned scoring means:
- risks can be compared consistently
- senior decision-makers understand what the ratings mean
- escalation thresholds are consistent
- risks aren't understated or overstated because different teams use different definitions
- security risks can feed into wider organisational risk management.
tasks: Do the scoring scales used for your service's security risk assessment align with your organisation's risk management processes?

actions.title: Do the scoring scales used for your service's security risk assessment align with your organisation's risk management processes?
actions.description:
• Identify the organisation's existing risk scoring framework.
• Use the same scales or establish a clear mapping between the security risk scale and organisational scale.
• Define what each likelihood, impact and severity rating means.
• Agree the scoring parameters with the appropriate risk/security stakeholders.
• Apply the scoring consistently across the service's security risks.
